title: MCP servers
lead: MCP servers give chat more tools, such as searching documentation, drawing charts or reading your issue tracker. Add a server here, then turn it on in a chat’s Plugins. Chat uses it only when a request needs it.
empty: You haven’t added a server yet. Add one with the command that starts it or its URL, or paste the configuration from its instructions.
tryExample: To try one, add Microsoft Learn, which searches Microsoft’s documentation, such as Fabric’s and Power BI’s.

card.checkTitle: Start or connect to it, and list its tools
card.confirmRemove: Remove {{name}}? Chats that have it on stop using it.
card.noTools: It connected, and offers no tools.
card.needsSignIn: It needs you to sign in. The first time a message in a chat uses it, Fabricator opens its sign-in page in your browser.

form.pasteHint: Paste the JSON from the server’s instructions, its command or its URL. Fabricator fills in the form for you to check.
form.choose: It has {{total}} servers. Choose the one to add:
form.name: Name
form.commandHint: The command that starts the server, with its arguments, as you’d type it in a terminal. Fabricator runs it on this computer, in the app’s folder.
form.sse: It uses Server-Sent Events (SSE), as some older servers do

secrets.windows: For keys and tokens. Fabricator keeps their values in Windows Credential Manager, not in its settings, and never shows them again.
secrets.mac: For keys and tokens. Fabricator keeps their values in your Keychain, not in its settings, and never shows them again.

form.readOnlyHint: Chat can call only the tools the server marks as read-only, so it can’t change anything with the server. In a team app, that’s always the case.
form.trust: A server runs with your access to this computer and your accounts, and what chat sends it leaves Fabricator. Add only servers you trust.

parse.unreadable: That isn’t a configuration Fabricator can read. Paste the JSON from the server’s instructions.
parse.noServer: That configuration doesn’t have a server with a command or a URL.
